newsitem.title: USA: OUTLOOK - U.S. products seen facing uphill battle.
newsitem.headline: OUTLOOK - U.S. products seen facing uphill battle.

text.p: U.S. cash refined products will likely face mounting downward price pressure this week, with gasoline especially susceptible to the armada of imports headed for New York Harbor, traders said Monday.

One East Coast player predicted gasoline will continue to lose ground as a dozen or more expected cargoes reach New York Harbor in the next two weeks and as traders try to unload barrels of summer-specification fuel. "A lot of people are trying to sell summer formulas because the switchover to (higher) reid vapor pressure fuels begins in mid-September."
Most gasoline grades settled 1.50 cents a gallon lower on Monday, tracking September NYMEX futures, with heating oil sliding almost a cent.
The NYMEX decline came on the heels of volatile NYMEX trade last week, where futures prices plumbed highs and lows on successive days leaving traders puzzled.

At the end of a week of whipsaw trading, gasoline emerged the clear loser Friday, with New York conventional unleaded "M2-grade" dropping 1.20 cents and U.S. Gulf conventional unleaded "M1" falling 0.70 cent.

Heating oil, bolstered by data showing total U.S. distillate stocks 18 million barrels shy of last year's levels, managed to eke a half-cent gain Friday after enduring similar roller-coaster price swings.
But traders said low seasonal demand for distillates will nevertheless continue to undermine prices this week.
"Most people will be looking for lower values," said Tom Knight, a senior trader for Fina Inc.
"The only salvation," he said, would be a move by Gulf refiners to cut their crude runs this week as a result of lower margins in the past 10 days.
"Over the longer term that would firm things in the Gulf," he said, but added curtailed runs probably would not help products prices until early to middle September.
"It would be gradual, like the way a snake moves -- the front part curves and eventually the tail."
By contrast, Purvin & Gertz Inc senior analyst Ken Miller said he believed refiners were likely to keep runs in high gear in order to maximize production of distillates.
Heating oil began commanding higher prices than gasoline on August 14, Miller said.
"The driving force for strong runs will be that heating oil has gotten ahead of gasoline and it's quite early in the year for that to happen," Miller said.

"It's going to be hard with strong crude runs to avoid ending up with excess gasoline," he added, putting more downward stress on gasoline as demand wanes with the approaching end of the summer driving season.
One trader active in the Group Three and Chicago markets predicted continued downward price pressures.
He cited recent discounting by one regional refiner and scheduled shipments due to arrive in the Midwest soon.

The Williams pipeline system, a key barometer of stocks in the region, reported supplies at 4.9 million barrels, or an ample 21 days worth of gasoline in its pipeline and storage network in the Midwest.
"We're going to be well supplied, so I would imagine basis is going to move lower on gasoline," a Midwest trader said.
--New York Energy Desk, 212 859-1620
